items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-D is marked full, but the linked test 'Should leave an existing service session in the cache and set or clear no service session cookie' (trade-imports-ins-frontend src/server/auth/idm-sign-in.test.js @97c72f1) seeds the session in the cache and never sends the service session cookie with the callback request. The GIVEN (user signed in through the service's own sign-in) is therefore not set up: a callback that read the incoming service cookie and dropped that session from the cache would still pass. Only the set-cookie half is proven.
items.fix: Must: the test linked as full for SCN-INS-AUTH-003-D sends the callback request with a real service session cookie for the cached session, so dropping or clearing that session turns it red; otherwise the link is marked partial. One way: build the cookie header with the existing address-book-requests helpers (cookieHeaderOf / a stub sign-in) and pass it in completeSignIn's headers.

items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-C says the page 'lists every ID token claim with its value' and 'every access token claim', but the links marked full/partial assert only claim names: the ID-token test uses arrayContaining(['aud','iss','sub','contactId']) on dt text (a subset, no dd values) and the access-token test checks only that 'scp' appears. A claimRows that rendered wrong or empty values, or dropped sessionId/correlationId, would pass while the coverage claims full.
items.fix: Must: the test linked as full for SCN-INS-AUTH-003-C asserts every ID token claim name paired with its rendered value (and likewise for access token claims), or the link's strength is lowered to partial. One way: compare the dt/dd pairs in [data-testid="id-token-claims"] to the signed token's payload with toEqual, and do the same for access-token-claims.

items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-B's first THEN ('it shows a button to sign in with Defra ID') is linked full to 'Should show a start page whose button links to the route that goes to IDM', which asserts only the button's href, never its text; the page could label the button anything and still pass.
items.fix: Must: the linked test asserts the start page's button text names signing in with Defra ID, or the link is marked partial. One way: add expect(textOf($, 'main a.govuk-button')).toBe(<the copy>) to that test.

items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E (lines 72-77) understates the AC 'An error from Defra ID is logged in full, and the user sees a generic error page': it specs only the generic page and says nothing of the log. The code does log (idm-sign-in.js completeSignIn: 'IDM sign-in failed' with err, idmError, idmErrorDescription, state; 'IDM ID token refused' with err), and other ins specs state logging in scenarios (address-book/spec.md:331, transporters/spec.md:228), so half the AC has no spec line and no coverage link.
items.fix: Must: the error scenario states that the full IDM error (error, description, state, or the token-refusal cause) is logged, as the address-book and transporters specs phrase logging, and the coverage row for it names a test that asserts the log or is marked partial/none until one does. One way: add '- **AND** the error is logged in full, with IDM's error, its description and the request state' to SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E and add a logger assertion to the 'returns an error' test in idm-sign-in.test.js.

items.issue: REQ-INS-AUTH-003 (line 40) says the service 'MUST NOT link to it from any other page', which is the AC 'Nothing in the INS frontend links to the hidden sign-in pages', but no scenario under it states that rule, so coverage.json rolls the requirement up to 'full' while this MUST has no scenario and no test behind it.
items.fix: Must: every MUST in REQ-INS-AUTH-003 is carried by a scenario, and the no-link rule's scenario has a coverage link or is recorded as none with a note. One way: add SCN-INS-AUTH-003-H 'No page of the service links to the IDM sign-in' (GIVEN IDM is configured, WHEN the user moves through the service's own pages, THEN none links to the IDM sign-in start, signed-in or signed-out pages) and add its coverage entry.

items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-F's title 'The signed-in page with no IDM sign-in starts one' (line 79) claims more than its THEN (line 83) and the code (showSignedIn redirects to idmPaths.signIn): the visitor is sent to the start page, and no sign-in at IDM starts until they press its button.
items.fix: Must: the scenario title says what the THEN says. One way: 'The signed-in page with no IDM sign-in sends the user to the start page'.

items.issue: Purpose (line 5) is now three sentences; openspec/config.yaml says 'Purpose: one or two sentences'. Separately, REQ-INS-AUTH-003's last sentence (line 40) 'It MUST NOT let the IDM identity reach any other page of the service, which keeps its own sign-in and that sign-in's data' attaches 'which' to 'the service', so it reads as a description rather than the second half of the rule.
items.fix: Must: Purpose is at most two sentences, and the requirement's last sentence states the rule unambiguously. One way: Purpose 'Signing in to the Import Notification Service, what an unauthenticated user reaching one of its pages gets instead, and a hidden sign-in through the real Defra ID (IDM) that shows what IDM returns without signing anyone in to the service.'; requirement 'The IDM identity MUST NOT reach any other page of the service: the service's own sign-in and its session stay as they were.'

items.issue: The Integrations table lists one identity provider, 'Defra ID (trade-imports-defra-id-stub locally) — OIDC (DEFRA_ID_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL)'. The service now also calls the real Defra ID (IDM) for discovery, JWKS and token exchange when IDM_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL is set, with metric dependency 'idm'.
items.fix: Must: the table lists the IDM integration. One way: add an Outbound row for Defra ID IDM in CP-Dev (IDM_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL, optional), OIDC, the hidden test sign-in at /auth/idm/sign-in that never signs anyone in to the service.

items.issue: Lines 15 and 17 say 'Sign-in and sign-out via Defra ID (OIDC)' and 'Routes are only registered when auth.enabled is true'. A second, hidden sign-in now exists, and its routes (/auth/idm/sign-in, /auth/idm/go-to-defra-id, /auth/callback, /auth/idm/signed-in, /auth/signed-out) are registered whatever auth.enabled is, gated only by IDM_OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL.
items.fix: Must: the Owns list states the hidden sign-in and when its routes exist. One way: one bullet under Owns.

items.issue: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-G says the post-logout page just 'says they have signed out', and SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E does not cover a refusal arriving there. Defra ID sends a refused sign-in to /auth/signed-out with error and error_description (routing proxy, EUDPA-806, README:137).
items.fix: Must: a scenario says that arriving at the post-logout page with an error shows the unable-to-sign-in page with a try-again link and logs the error, and its coverage links the test. One way: add a GIVEN variant to SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E, or a new scenario under REQ-INS-AUTH-003.

items.issue: One rule, 2 findings: #4, trade-imports-ins-frontend #33 — the AC 'An error from Defra ID is logged in full' is neither in the spec (SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E names only the page) nor proven by a test (deleting the logger calls leaves idm-sign-in.test.js green).
items.fix: Must: SCN-INS-AUTH-003-E states the error is logged in full, a test in idm-sign-in.test.js asserts the log, and coverage links that test. One way: add the AND line to the scenario and a logger assertion to the 'returns an error' test.
